text:
Sam: Heads-up — after landing the kernel-selector tweak yesterday we're seeing a ~15-20% p95 latency regression on long-seq (2k+) workloads :eyes:
Anya: ugh. Which tweak exactly? the preference for the new wide-kernel path?
Sam: yeah the change that prefers fast_wide for seq>1024. Regression shows up in perf dashboards around 09:12UTC. I grabbed nsys traces before/after.
Sam: pre/post profiler commands I ran:
```bash
# pre-change baseline
nsys profile -o pre_trace -t cuda,cudnn,osrt -- ./bench_infer --model redwood-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1
# post-change (after kernel selector commit)
nsys profile -o post_trace -t cuda,cudnn,osrt -- ./bench_infer --model redwood-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1
```
Sam: quick summary from flame counts (sampled from timeline):
- pre: attn_fused ~42%, matmul_k ~18%, prefetch ~5%, memcpy ~4%
- post: memcpy_async ~28%, prefetch_v2 ~22%, attn_fused ~30%
Anya: memcpy_async jumping that much smells like a change that increased KV cache churn or introduced extra host->device copies. Did you capture kernel names/stream ids?
Sam: yes — post trace shows a new prefetch kernel on stream 6 that runs before attn and issues batched cudaMemcpyAsync calls. The selector picked a kernel variant that doesn't use the existing KV pinned-cache path, so we end up staging keys.
Cheng: can you paste the snippet from nvprof/nsys showing the top kernels?
Sam: pasted below from nsys export summary:
```
# pre_trace top 5:
attn_fused          42.1%  total time
matmul_k            18.3%
kv_read_prefetch     5.2%
memcpy_async         4.0%
other                30.4%
# post_trace top 5:
memcpy_async         28.6%
prefetch_v2          22.7%
attn_fused           30.1%
matmul_k             10.3%
other                8.3%
```
Lina: that explains p95. Async memcpy increases overlap but also adds serialization when it blocks on page faults or when pinned memory isn't used. Did the selector change touch prefetch flags or cache alloc path?
Sam: the commit altered kernel preference table and toggled the "use_kv_pinned_path" heuristic for some variants — but I don't see an explicit pinned flag in the new variant. It seems the wide kernel assumes ephemeral KV buffers.
Cheng: can we reproduce with env override? try forcing legacy selector to confirm cause:
```bash
REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy ./bench_infer --model redwood-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --trace nsight
```
Sam: did that — legacy selector restores pre-change profile and p95 back to baseline. So it's definitely selector-related.
perf-ci-bot: starting bisect across commits 6a1f..d3c9 to find first bad commit. See: https://ci.redwood/prof/bisect/2630001111
Anya: nice. If bisect points to the variant table tweak, we can either revert or update the variant to use the pinned KV path. Which is less risky?
Lina: updating variant to reuse pinned KV path is preferable long-term. We should add a unit/regression test that runs a short nsys profile on the slow path to catch this.
Cheng: small experiment idea — run workload with small seq (512) and long seq (2048) and compare kernel timeline gaps. Also capture perfetto timeline to see inter-stream blocking.
Sam: did perfetto snapshot; found that the prefetch_v2 kernels are launched earlier but they wait on a host-side barrier where memcpy stalls for ~6-8ms intermittently. That aligns with page migration or unpinned allocation.
Anya: did the change also alter allocator flags? Maybe new kernel requests unpinned malloc for KV scratch. Check allocator logs with REDWOOD_ALLOC_DEBUG=1.
Sam: allocator shows the new path calls malloc (not cudaHostAlloc) for KV buffers. So yes — unpinned.
Cheng: ok root cause = selector chose variant that uses unpinned KV staging -> increased memcpy_async time -> p95 regression on long seq. Bisect should point to the selector commit.
perf-ci-bot: bisect finished. First bad commit: abc1234 — "prefer fast_wide kernel for long sequences". See details: https://ci.redwood/commit/abc1234
Sam: plan: revert selector preference in abc1234 for now, and create follow-up to update the wide kernel to use pinned KV path. I'll open PR to revert to restore perf ASAP.
Lina: also add regression test that runs a mini nsys profile on 2k seq nightly and fails on memcpy% > 15%.
Anya: ACK. Can someone own the variant patch to add pinned allocations? Cheng?
Cheng: I can take that. Will prototype pinned KV path in a branch and run perf comparisons.
Sam: thanks — steps: 1) revert selector pref (PR up in 10m), 2) nightly regression test, 3) variant patch to use cudaHostAlloc, 4) re-enable selector after validation.
Lina: add a small changelog note and mark the incident in postmortems channel.
Sam: filing follow-ups now. TL;DR: kernel selector introduced a variant that avoids pinned KV, causing memcpy_async hotspot and 15-20% p95 regression; bisect points to abc1234; revert+patch planned. :white_check_mark:
